title: Measuring the bumps: volatility, beta, Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown
objectives: Explain volatility, standard deviation, beta and drawdown in plain words.
Say what Sharpe and Sortino ratios reward, and why higher is better.
body_md:
Volatility is how much and how often returns swing. Standard deviation puts a number on it: higher means bigger swings around the average. Beta measures movement against the benchmark: beta 1.2 means the fund tends to move about 12% when the market moves 10%. Sharpe ratio is return above the risk-free rate per unit of total volatility; Sortino counts only downside volatility. Drawdown is the fall from a peak to a low before recovering.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard deviation | A number for volatility: higher means bigger swings around the average | SD 20% vs 12%: the first fund is bumpier |
| Beta | How much a fund moves compared with its benchmark | Beta 1.2: if the market moves 10%, the fund tends to move about 12% |
| Sharpe ratio | Return earned above a risk-free rate for each unit of total volatility. Higher is better | Two funds with the same return: the one with the higher Sharpe took a smoother road |
| Sortino ratio | Like Sharpe, but counts only downside volatility | Useful for clients who only worry about falls |
| Drawdown | Fall from a peak to a low before recovering | Portfolio at ₹10 lakh falls to ₹7 lakh → 30% drawdown |
example: A portfolio at ₹10 lakh falls to ₹7 lakh: that is a 30% drawdown. The question is whether the client could sit through it without selling.
say: Two funds with the same return: the one with the higher Sharpe took a smoother road.
A beta above 1 means the fund is more sensitive than the market.
never: A high Sharpe ratio means guaranteed returns.
Volatility and loss are the same thing.

check.q: A beta of 1.2 means the fund tends to move:
check.why: About 20% more than the market. Beta above 1 = more sensitive than the market.
